text: What is weather?
choices: The short-term state of the atmosphere
The average climate over centuries
The solid interior of Earth
The daily motion of ocean tides

text: In which atmospheric layer does most everyday weather occur?
choices: The stratosphere
The troposphere
The mesosphere
The thermosphere

text: Which cloud type forms broad, fairly uniform gray layers?
choices: Cumulus
Cirrus
Stratus
Altocumulus

text: What appearance is typical of fair-weather cumulus clouds?
choices: Thin icy feathers high in the sky
A uniform dark sheet at ground level
Rotating funnels reaching the surface
Puffy, detached heaps with relatively flat bases

text: Which clouds are thin and wispy and usually found at high altitude?
choices: Cirrus
Stratus
Nimbostratus
Cumulonimbus

text: Which cloud is most strongly associated with thunderstorms?
choices: Cirrostratus
Cumulonimbus
Altostratus
Stratocumulus

text: What kind of precipitation is commonly produced by nimbostratus clouds?
choices: Only small hailstones
Dust and sand
Steady widespread rain or snow
No precipitation at all

text: What does humidity measure?
choices: The speed of a storm
The amount of sunlight at noon
The salt content of rain
The amount of water vapor in the air

text: What is the dew point?
choices: The temperature at which air becomes saturated with water vapor
The highest temperature of the day
The point where wind stops
The height of a cloud base above sea level

text: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
choices: An anemometer
A barometer
A hygrometer
A pyranometer

text: What does a thermometer measure in weather observing?
choices: Wind direction
Cloud height
Air temperature
Rain acidity

text: Which instrument measures wind speed?
choices: A barometer
A rain gauge
A ceilometer
An anemometer

text: What does a wind vane indicate?
choices: Wind direction
Wind temperature
Cloud thickness
Air pressure

text: Which instrument collects and measures liquid precipitation?
choices: A radiosonde
A rain gauge
A barograph
A wind profiler

text: What does a hygrometer measure?
choices: Visibility
Pressure
Humidity
Solar radiation

text: What is a cold front?
choices: A stationary region with no temperature difference
The center of a hurricane
A high-altitude cloud boundary
The leading edge of advancing colder air

text: What usually happens as a warm front passes?
choices: Warmer air gradually replaces cooler air
Cold air suddenly replaces warm air
The wind always becomes calm
All cloud cover immediately disappears

text: What is a stationary front?
choices: A front found only over oceans
A boundary that moves very little
A front with hurricane-force winds
A boundary between day and night

text: What is an occluded front?
choices: A front that produces only sunshine
A front found exclusively at the equator
A front formed when one moving front overtakes another
A boundary created by ocean tides

text: What weather is often associated with a broad high-pressure system?
choices: Persistent rising air and thunderstorms everywhere
A guaranteed blizzard
Only dense fog at noon
Generally sinking air and fairer conditions

text: What weather is commonly associated with a low-pressure system?
choices: Rising air and increased cloud or precipitation
Clear skies caused by sinking air
No wind under any circumstances
Permanent dry heat

text: What are isobars on a weather map?
choices: Lines connecting equal rainfall
Lines connecting equal air pressure
Lines marking cloud tops
Lines showing ocean salinity

text: What does precipitation include?
choices: Only liquid rain
Only water vapor
Water falling from clouds as rain, snow, sleet, or hail
Sunlight reflected by clouds

text: What is hail?
choices: Frozen fog at the ground
Snow melted into rain
Salt crystals blown from beaches
Balls or lumps of ice formed in strong thunderstorms

text: What is freezing rain?
choices: Liquid rain that freezes on contact with cold surfaces
Snow that never reaches the ground
Rain that falls only in summer
Hail smaller than a pea

text: What process changes liquid water into water vapor?
choices: Condensation
Evaporation
Deposition
Runoff

text: What process forms cloud droplets when water vapor cools?
choices: Evaporation
Sublimation
Condensation
Infiltration

text: Why does rising air often cool in the atmosphere?
choices: It absorbs heat from the stratosphere
It becomes heavier as it rises
It loses all water vapor instantly
It expands as surrounding pressure decreases

text: What is a sea breeze?
choices: A daytime wind blowing from sea toward warmer land
A nighttime wind from land toward sea
A wind found only during hurricanes
A high-altitude jet stream

text: What is a land breeze?
choices: A daytime wind from ocean to beach
A nighttime wind blowing from cooler land toward the sea
A wind that circles a tornado
A wind caused by mountain glaciers only

text: What causes thunder?
choices: Clouds colliding in the upper atmosphere
Rain striking the ocean
The rapid expansion of air heated by lightning
Ice crystals rubbing against mountains

text: What is lightning?
choices: A reflection of sunlight from hail
A column of falling snow
A pressure line on a weather map
A large electrical discharge in the atmosphere

text: What is the calm central region of a mature hurricane called?
choices: The eye
The eyewall
The rainband
The outflow jet

text: Where are a hurricane's strongest sustained winds usually found?
choices: In the eye
In the eyewall
Far above the tropopause
Only in the outermost cloud tops

text: What is the rotating column of air associated with a tornado called?
choices: An isobar
A monsoon
A vortex
A frontolysis zone

text: Which scale is used in the United States to rate tornado damage intensity?
choices: The Saffir-Simpson scale
The Beaufort scale
The Fujita-Saffir index
The Enhanced Fujita scale

text: What is a blizzard in the usual North American definition?
choices: A snowstorm with strong winds and severely reduced visibility
Any snowfall lasting more than one hour
A rainstorm with thunder
A tropical cyclone over cold water

text: What is a monsoon?
choices: A single violent thunderstorm
A seasonal reversal in prevailing winds, often bringing a wet season
A permanent wind at the poles
A type of high cloud

text: What does El Niño describe in the tropical Pacific?
choices: Unusually cold Atlantic waters
A daily reversal of mountain winds
Unusually warm central and eastern surface waters
A permanent shift of Earth's axis

text: What does La Niña describe in the tropical Pacific?
choices: Unusually warm Arctic waters
A dust storm over Australia
A weakening of all trade winds
Unusually cool central and eastern surface waters

text: What is the jet stream?
choices: A narrow band of fast winds high in the atmosphere
A wind that occurs only inside tornadoes
A surface current in the ocean
A stream of falling precipitation

text: What does a weather forecast attempt to predict?
choices: The exact climate of a century
Future atmospheric conditions
The orbit of a satellite only
The chemical composition of rocks

text: What is a weather radar primarily used to detect?
choices: Air temperature inside buildings
Ocean depth
Precipitation and its movement
The composition of the stratosphere

text: What does a weather satellite observe from orbit?
choices: Only underground water
The wind inside every home
Earthquake waves beneath the seafloor
Clouds, moisture, and atmospheric patterns

text: What is the main difference between a weather warning and a watch in U.S. terminology?
choices: A warning means hazardous weather is occurring or imminent, while a watch means conditions are favorable
A watch always means greater danger than a warning
A warning applies only to winter, while a watch applies only to summer
They are identical terms used by different airports

text: What is fog?
choices: Smoke produced by a wildfire
A cloud at or very near the ground
Rain that falls only at night
A layer of ice crystals in the stratosphere

text: What is an anvil top on a thunderstorm cloud?
choices: The rotating center at the surface
A narrow rain shaft beneath a cloud
The flattened, spreading top formed near the tropopause
A layer of fog inside the eye

text: What does visibility report in a weather observation?
choices: The height of the highest cloud
The speed of a storm's movement
The amount of water in the soil
The greatest distance at which objects can be clearly seen

text: In common North American usage, what is sleet?
choices: Small ice pellets that fall from a winter cloud
Freezing fog on a runway
Liquid rain that freezes on contact
Large balls of thunderstorm ice

text: What is a weather station?
choices: A television channel that broadcasts forecasts
A site equipped to measure atmospheric conditions
A satellite orbit used for climate models
A building where only radar is manufactured

text: Which atmospheric boundary separates the troposphere from the stratosphere?
choices: The mesopause
The stratopause
The tropopause
The ionopause

text: What generally happens to temperature with height through the troposphere?
choices: It increases uniformly
It remains exactly constant
It alternates every kilometer
It decreases on average

text: What does CAPE estimate in convective weather analysis?
choices: The buoyant energy available to rising air
The amount of rain already measured
The speed of a surface cold front
The height of the tropopause only

text: What does convective inhibition, or CIN, represent?
choices: The maximum wind speed in a hurricane
Energy that suppresses a parcel's initial upward motion
The electrical charge of a cloud
The amount of ice in a snowpack

text: What does a negative lifted index generally suggest?
choices: A completely stable atmosphere
Freezing rain at the surface
An atmosphere favorable for instability and convection
A lack of moisture at all levels

text: Why is vertical wind shear important in severe-storm forecasting?
choices: It determines the salinity of precipitation
It prevents all cloud formation
It measures the depth of the ocean
Changing wind with height can organize and sustain rotating storms

text: What apparent deflection of moving air results from Earth's rotation?
choices: The Coriolis effect
The greenhouse effect
The rain-shadow effect
The Bernoulli effect

text: What is a geostrophic wind in an idealized atmosphere?
choices: A wind driven only by local heating
A wind balanced mainly by pressure-gradient and Coriolis forces
A wind that always blows downhill
A wind found only in tropical cyclones

text: What are Rossby waves?
choices: Tiny ripples on raindrops
Waves generated only by ocean tides
Large-scale meanders in the midlatitude westerly flow
Circular waves around tornado funnels

text: What is a jet-streak entrance or exit region useful for identifying?
choices: The exact location of a surface rain gauge
The salinity of an atmospheric river
The freezing point of hail
Areas of upper-level divergence or convergence that can support vertical motion

text: What does positive relative vorticity describe?
choices: Counterclockwise rotation in the Northern Hemisphere convention
Only downward motion in thunderstorms
A decrease in atmospheric moisture
Wind blowing directly from east to west everywhere

text: What does QPF stand for in operational forecasting?
choices: Quick Pressure Field
Quantitative Precipitation Forecast
Qualified Polar Front
Quasi-Persistent Fog

text: What is numerical weather prediction?
choices: Guessing weather from folklore alone
Measuring rain with a manual gauge
Using computer models of atmospheric physics to calculate future conditions
Recording only past temperatures

text: Why are ensemble forecasts useful?
choices: They guarantee one exact forecast
They replace all observations
They measure only yesterday's weather
They show a range of outcomes from slightly different model states or assumptions

text: What does nowcasting usually cover?
choices: Very short-range prediction over the next few hours
Climate projections for centuries
Ocean tides over decades
Astronomical forecasts for eclipses

text: What does radar reflectivity mainly indicate?
choices: The direction of upper-level winds directly
The strength of returned energy from targets such as precipitation
The temperature of the ocean floor
The concentration of atmospheric oxygen

text: What does Doppler radar velocity estimate?
choices: The total rainfall depth in a season
The altitude of every cloud exactly
The component of target motion toward or away from the radar
The air pressure at the surface

text: What is the radar bright band?
choices: A ring around every tornado
A radar shadow behind a mountain
An area with no precipitation
A band of enhanced echoes near the melting layer where snow becomes rain

text: What radar signature can suggest a supercell's mesocyclone?
choices: A persistent velocity couplet showing adjacent inbound and outbound motion
A perfectly circular area of weak reflectivity at every elevation
A straight line of only light rain
A bright band below the surface

text: What is a bow echo?
choices: A curved cloud around a hurricane eye
A bow-shaped line of thunderstorms often associated with strong straight-line winds
A rainbow visible in radar data
A snow band caused by lake effect only

text: What is a supercell?
choices: Any thunderstorm with hail
A storm above the stratosphere
A thunderstorm with a persistent rotating updraft
A tropical cyclone over land

text: What is a mesocyclone?
choices: The calm center of a hurricane
A low-pressure center at the ocean surface
A wave in the jet stream
A rotating updraft region within a severe thunderstorm

text: What is an eyewall replacement cycle?
choices: A tropical cyclone process in which a new outer eyewall contracts around the old one
A hurricane changing its name at landfall
A daily switch between tropical and extratropical status
The replacement of a storm's forecast model

text: What does rapid intensification mean for a tropical cyclone?
choices: A storm moving quickly across the ocean
A substantial increase in maximum sustained winds over a short period
A cyclone weakening after landfall
A change from a watch to a warning

text: What does the Saffir-Simpson scale classify for Atlantic hurricanes?
choices: Total storm rainfall only
The diameter of the eye
Category based on maximum sustained wind speed
The number of tornadoes produced

text: What is storm surge?
choices: A wave caused only by an earthquake
A sudden increase in rainfall over mountains
A tide that occurs every afternoon
An abnormal rise of seawater driven mainly by a storm's winds and pressure

text: What is an atmospheric river?
choices: A long, narrow corridor transporting large amounts of water vapor
A permanent river flowing through the stratosphere
A line of tornadoes over the ocean
A radar beam aimed at the equator

text: What is orographic precipitation?
choices: Rain caused by an urban heat island only
Precipitation produced when terrain forces moist air upward
Snow formed solely by lake evaporation
Precipitation from a tropical cyclone's eye

text: What is a rain shadow?
choices: A dark cloud that blocks sunlight
A radar gap caused by heavy rain
A relatively dry region on the leeward side of a mountain range
A daily shadow cast by a thunderstorm

text: What is a foehn wind?
choices: A cold sea breeze at sunset
A circular wind inside a hurricane eye
A high-altitude polar easterly
A warm, dry downslope wind on the lee side of mountains

text: What is a temperature inversion?
choices: A layer in which temperature increases with height instead of decreasing
A sudden reversal of the seasons
A cloud that changes into rain
A switch from Celsius to Fahrenheit

text: What does infrared satellite imagery help meteorologists estimate?
choices: The exact wind speed at every surface point
Cloud-top temperature and related cloud height
The salinity of seawater
The chemical composition of hailstones

text: What does water-vapor satellite imagery emphasize?
choices: Only liquid water on the ground
The depth of underground aquifers
The distribution and motion of moisture in selected atmospheric layers
The reflectivity of snow on roads

text: What is a radiosonde?
choices: A satellite that maps ocean currents
A radar dish mounted on a ship
A sensor buried beneath snow
An instrument package carried aloft by a weather balloon

text: What does an atmospheric sounding provide?
choices: A vertical profile of variables such as temperature, moisture, pressure, and wind
A map of only surface rainfall
A record of ocean tides
A list of historical hurricane names

text: Why does higher model resolution often help forecast local weather features?
choices: It eliminates atmospheric chaos
Smaller grid spacing can represent finer terrain and storm structures
It makes observations unnecessary
It guarantees perfect precipitation timing

text: What does ensemble spread generally indicate?
choices: The width of a hurricane's eyewall only
The distance between weather stations
How much forecast solutions differ from one another
The thickness of a cloud layer

text: Why do forecasts become less certain farther into the future?
choices: The atmosphere stops being measurable after one day
Weather satellites turn off at night
Air pressure becomes constant globally
Small initial errors can grow in a chaotic atmosphere

text: What does dual-polarization radar add compared with conventional reflectivity alone?
choices: Information about target shape and type, improving precipitation identification
A direct measurement of lightning voltage
A map of underground faults
A forecast of next year's climate

text: What is a tropical cyclone called in the western North Pacific?
choices: A willy-willy
A typhoon
A baguio
A pampero

text: What is a tropical cyclone called in the North Atlantic and eastern North Pacific?
choices: A typhoon
A cyclone only
A hurricane
A norther

text: What is a cold pool in a thunderstorm system?
choices: The frozen center of a hurricane
A layer of cold ocean water beneath the thermocline
A cloud-free area above a jet streak
A spreading region of cooled air produced by precipitation and downdrafts

text: What is a gust front?
choices: The leading edge of thunderstorm outflow spreading along the surface
The strongest wind around a hurricane eye
A boundary between two ocean currents
The front edge of a snowplow

text: What is the hook echo on weather radar commonly associated with?
choices: A mature hurricane eye only
A rotating supercell that may contain a tornado
A band of light stratiform rain
A clear-air temperature inversion

text: What is the main forecasting significance of a dryline in the Great Plains of the United States?
choices: It marks the boundary between snow and sea ice
It is a permanent high-pressure ridge
It separates moist Gulf air from much drier air and can focus thunderstorms
It is a line of ocean fog

text: What is wind chill intended to describe?
choices: The actual measured air temperature
The total heat stored in a hurricane
The speed of wind at the tropopause
How cold moving air makes exposed skin feel compared with calm air

text: What is distinctive about a geostationary weather satellite's orbit?
choices: It appears fixed over one longitude while orbiting with Earth's rotation
It passes over both poles on every orbit
It remains directly above the North Pole
It travels only beneath the atmosphere

text: Why is potential vorticity useful in dynamic meteorology?
choices: It measures only the amount of rain in a cloud
It combines rotational and stratification information and is conserved in idealized flow
It gives the exact number of tornadoes in a storm
It identifies the chemical composition of aerosols

text: How does the moist-adiabatic lapse rate differ from the dry-adiabatic rate?
choices: A saturated parcel always warms faster than the surrounding air
It applies only below the ocean surface
A saturated parcel usually cools more slowly because condensation releases latent heat
It is exactly the same at every temperature

text: What is a baroclinic zone?
choices: A calm area at the center of a tropical cyclone
A radar blind spot caused by mountains
A layer made entirely of ice crystals
A region where pressure surfaces and density or temperature surfaces are not parallel
